note: The OLG Categorical Eligibility page thoroughly covers the policy substance of FNS 1061.3. The OLG explicitly states that PA households are 'considered to have automatically passed a SNAP gross income test, net income test and/or asset test' — directly addressing the FNS requirement that CE households are eligible regardless of income. The 'Categorically Eligible Households' section further specifies that CE households are approved even when income exceeds limits (1-2 person HH receives minimum benefit, 3+ approved at $0). The 'Who Is Not Categorically Eligible' section lists the prohibited member exceptions (IPV, work program non-compliance, over-income elder/disabled HHs), which aligns with FNS's reference to Section 841 prohibitions. The IPV Overview page reinforces this: 'Households cannot be considered categorically eligible if they contain one or more disqualified members.' The remaining FNS requirements — that QC cannot remove CE conferment, that an allotment test must always be performed, how to handle PA households with excess income, and how to handle incorrect CE classification — are QC review procedures, not caseworker policy. The OLG does address the caseworker-relevant equivalent (BEACON auto-converts cases that lose CE status mid-certification and prompts asset verification).
